questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035973/assets/a0674c068305434109322c2ade681279f11b78944356d7663198f9bfbf9cf962.png)

Let $U={10,20,30,40,50}$ be the universal set and let $Q={10,30,40}.$ What is $\overset{―}{Q}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The complement of $Q,$ denoted $\overset{―}{Q},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $Q.$ To represent $\overset{―}{Q},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $Q,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035973/assets/a29068d63563404b495e603e473a990186fed086439318d9ac26685b9474f331.png)

The elements in the shaded area are $20$ and $50.$ These are the elements of $U$ that are not in $Q.$ Therefore, the complement of $Q$ is

$$
\overset{―}{Q}={20,50}.
$$
